 LaMelo Ball (wrist) and Terrence Shannon (hip) are questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Bucks. 
 With Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) sidelined, the Wolves’ backcourt could be thin on Monday. If Ball and/or Shannon sit out, more minutes would be available for Bones Hyland and Ayo Dosunmu. 
 Anthony Edwards 
 MIN 
 Guard 
 #5 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Anthony Edwards (knee) will undergo arthroscopic surgery and will miss up to two months. 
 So much for Edwards being listed as questionable on the Timberwolves’ initial injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. He’ll reportedly need to undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and could miss up to two months. While the timeline isn’t guaranteed, fantasy managers can stash Edwards on the IL until he’s cleared to return. As alternatives, Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon Jr. should see more opportunities, and starters Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga should too. 
 Anthony Edwards 
 MIN 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Anthony Edwards (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Despite dealing with a sore right knee, Edwards played 41 minutes in Monday’s overtime loss to the Cavaliers. Minnesota has another back-to-back on Friday/Saturday, so Edwards may get a day off at some point. If so, Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon Jr. would take on larger roles. 
 Terrence Shannon 
 MIN 
 Guard-Forward 
 #4 
 Terrence Shannon Jr. accounted for 15 points (5-of-6 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors. 
 The Timberwolves’ bench accounted for 41 of the team’s 117 points, led by Shannon with 15. He’s scored in double figures in all three of Minnesota’s games, but he still has work to do to become a reliable option in category leagues. Ayo Dosunmu (9/3/3 with one three-pointer) remains the better option for fantasy managers looking for value on the Timberwolves bench, even after a quiet night against the Raptors. 
 Cody Williams 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Cody Williams accounted for six points (2-of-3 FGs), one rebound, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s exhibition against the Knicks. 
 Jonathan Kuminga was unavailable for Monday’s exhibition, so Williams took the starting lineup spot. He didn’t provide much offensively, but the Timberwolves didn’t need him to. Williams spent a considerable amount of time guarding Jalen Brunson, and proving that he can contribute defensively may be the former Jazz forward’s path to rotation minutes. 
 Terrence Shannon 
 MIN 
 Guard-Forward 
 #4 
 Terrence Shannon Jr. recorded 19 points (8-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Saturday’s exhibition against the Heat. 
 Shannon started Saturday’s exhibition and played well, making half his shots and dishing out four assists. The third-year wing, who committed just one turnover, had his moments during the postseason last spring as the Timberwolves had to navigate multiple injuries. Shannon isn’t a must-draft player in 12-team redraft leagues, but the upside makes him worth considering in the final rounds. 
 Cody Williams 
 MIN 
 Forward 
 Timberwolves acquired Cody Williams and John Konchar from the Jazz for Josh Green. 
 The Timberwolves made this deal to free up cap space, likely to sign a veteran who’s a good locker-room presence. The tenth overall pick in the 2024 draft, Williams struggled to carve out a role for himself as a rookie but did show signs of improvement last season. Starting 41 of the 67 games he appeared in, the 6-foot-7 wing averaged 8.8 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 24.3 minutes in 2025-26. Adding Williams gives the Timberwolves a little more depth on the wing, but it will be challenging for him to land a role that will make him fantasy-relevant. 
 Cody Williams 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Cody Williams finished with 16 points (6-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, four steals, one block and two three-pointers against the Wizards on Thursday. 
 Though he clearly isn’t a finished product, Williams has shown progress entering his third season. He looks like how a third-year NBA player should look in summer league. Williams was solid in this game and should be a rotation piece for Utah this season, though the amount of depth they have may make it difficult for him to carve out a large role. 
 Cody Williams 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Cody Williams notched 18 points (7-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Grizzlies. 
 Williams entered the offseason with two directives: get stronger and improve defensively. He’s reportedly added 10 pounds to his frame, and the Jazz forward had an excellent all-around performance on Monday. After committing six turnovers in Saturday’s summer opener, Williams committed two against the Grizzlies and shot over 50 percent from the field. With the Jazz focused on actually competing next season, Williams’ margin for error is likely to be slim if he’s to earn rotation minutes. As for the rest of this summer, Utah’s decision-makers likely hope that he’ll show early in Las Vegas that he’s too good to be playing. 
 Cody Williams 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Cody Williams contributed 17 points (8-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks, one three-pointer and six turnovers against the Hawks on Saturday. 
 Third-year players should dominate summer league if they play, and Williams was able to show plenty of growth, even if he wasn’t perfect. The turnovers were frustrating for an experienced player, but he was able to score effectively, which included some ferocious dunks. Williams is still fighting for a place in the Jazz rotation this season, but this was an encouraging start to the summer for him.
